spec_match.rationale: Probes the exact new surface (getStats on WebTransport.prototype, descriptor, zero arity) and runs the spec algorithm's two failure moments — connecting-then-wait and failed-rejects-immediately — against a real doomed session.

interactive.rationale: Live descriptor readout on load plus a one-press run that constructs a real session and shows both settled outcomes with a timestamped step log.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Index blurb promises the descriptor probe and both verbatim settled outcomes with timestamps; the page delivers exactly that.

edge_cases.rationale: Covers no-WebTransport, method-missing (pre-159/unflagged), a pending-3s-after-failure out-of-contract branch, an unexpected ready-resolution branch, and labels Chromium's own 'retreive' typo as Chromium's.

references.rationale: Links chromestatus.com/feature/5120203192139776 and the exact spec anchor for getStats() in see-also.

conformance.rationale: Feature suite asserts the method's existence, own-descriptor shape, zero arity, Promise return, and both InvalidStateError failure contracts; executed live on the /conformance/ route: 0 pass / 6 fail unflagged (honest), 6 pass / 0 fail behind --enable-blink-features=WebTransportStats on Chromium 153.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Verified on headless Chrome for Testing 153.0.8010.12 (chrome-devtools-mcp unavailable in this cloud environment; Playwright-driven CDP over the real binary per the routine's headless fallback) at desktop 1280x800 and mobile 360x740 DPR3, unflagged AND behind WebTransportStats. Flagged: both moments rejected InvalidStateError 'Cannot retreive stats on a failed connection.' in ~30ms; unflagged: honest method-missing branch. Screenshots read for both classes; zero page errors; the only console noise is the intentional dead-endpoint QUIC failure, recorded as an expected handled network failure.

telemetry_health.rationale: Asserts wt-stats-probe-surface on load and wt-stats-probe-failed-branch-invalidstate / wt-stats-probe-missing-branch / wt-stats-probe-fallback per branch; console output is intentional and prefixed [wt-stats:probe].

design_system.rationale: Only CSS variables from public/styles.css; buttons overriding background also set color; verdict/result colours (accent-emerald-dark, accent-rose) sit on near-white surfaces at AA.

accessibility.rationale: Native button with a descriptive name, kv list in dl semantics, aria-live=polite on the verdict, step log and output; moment results are plain text, not colour-only (state word 'rejected:'/'resolved with' leads each line); visible focus from the shared stylesheet verified on first Tab.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Both viewports exercised with the full control sequence; the kv grid collapses to one column under 480px; driver asserted no horizontal overflow on either class.

openQuestions.title: Re-verify both moments and the resolved path on a real Chrome 159 build
openQuestions.detail: This environment verified the failure moments behind the WebTransportStats flag on Chromium 153. On an actual Chrome 159 (unflagged) build, confirm the probe verdict flips without the flag, and use the live-stats monitor against a reachable endpoint to confirm the resolved path that this page deliberately does not fake.

guidanceConsulted.query: accessible status updates live region after button action
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Surface async state changes through polite live regions attached to semantic output elements, with text that does not rely on colour alone.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Verdict, step log and summary use aria-live=polite; settled outcomes lead with the words 'rejected:'/'resolved with' so colour is redundant.

guidanceConsulted.query: responsive data table narrow mobile no horizontal overflow
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use intrinsic grids and overflow-wrap so key/value readouts reflow instead of overflowing at narrow widths.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: dl.kv collapses to one column below 480px and uses overflow-wrap:anywhere; verified no horizontal overflow at 360px DPR3.

summary: Exact-surface probe plus the spec's two failure moments run against a real doomed session; on flagged Chromium 153 both moments rejected InvalidStateError exactly as the spec algorithm requires, and every unsupported branch labels itself honestly.
